chunks: And with this chain of transmission—I mean the first chain—from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who became junub, then performed tayammum with earth and prayed, then afterward found water,
So he said: “He does not repeat. Indeed, the Lord of water is the Lord of earth; thus he has performed one of the two means of taharah (ritual purification).”

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became in a state of janabah requiring ritual purification
key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: earth, the material used for tayammum
key_terms.الطَّهُورَيْنِ: the two valid means of ritual purification, namely water and earth
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the normal means of purification
key_terms.بِالصَّعِيدِ: with earth or clean ground used for tayammum
key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.لَا يُعِيدُ: he does not repeat the prayer

ai.seo_question: If a person in janabah performs tayammum and prays, then later finds water, must he repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on tayammum for one in janabah who prayed after performing dry ablution and later found water. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that the prayer does not need to be repeated, because tayammum is a valid form of taharah when water is unavailable.
